findings.title: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` grants manage permission when the caller only has `view` scope on all-groups
findings.body: In `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` (line 70, and documented in `GroupPermissionEvaluator` line 75), `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` is called, which checks whether the caller has either `view` OR `manage` permission on the all-groups resource. Because `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` calls `auth.groups().requireManage()`, any user granted only the `view` scope on the `Groups` resource type can create or move top-level groups in the realm. `canManage()` should only check `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE`.

findings.title: `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` in `GroupPermissionsV2` does not match group resources and returns resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: In `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` (lines 121-125): (1) `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` only finds resources whose `type` is set to `"Groups"`. However, `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` never sets the resource type on individual group resources when creating them (only the all-groups resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` has `type = "Groups"`). (2) Inside the callback, `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` is called, but `hasPermission` looks up the resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` where the resource's `name` is the group's ID (not `groupResource.getId()`). (3) `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` adds the authorization resource's internal ID rather than the `GroupModel` ID (`groupResource.getName()`). As a result, `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` will never return the actual group IDs, breaking user search and user count filtering by group view permissions in FGAP V2.

findings.title: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName` does not handle `GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE`
findings.body: In `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName` (lines 328-350), only `USERS` is handled to translate a resource name (which stores the entity ID) into a human-readable name. For `GROUPS`, individual group resources are created with `name = group.getId()` and no display name, so `getResourceName` falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()` and returns `null` (or the raw resource name for the `Groups` resource-type resource instead of a label like `"All groups"`).
